title: Research brief
summary: A short sourced answer in Markdown: every claim cites a source, every cited page was archived and resolves, and every quoted passage is in the archived page.

criteria.label: Has a Question section, a Findings section with claims, and a Sources section with [S1] <url> "quote" lines
Every claim in Findings ends with a citation that is listed in Sources
Every cited URL has an archived record with a 2xx status
Every quoted passage is found in the archived page it is attributed to
The findings answer the question that was asked

anchors.1: The findings are about something else, or are so general that they could answer any question on the topic.
anchors.3: The findings address the question and give a usable answer. Part of it is missing, vague or only implied.
anchors.5: The findings answer the question directly and completely, and a reader could act on them without searching further.

examples.1: The question asks which field a standard requires. The findings describe the standard's history.
examples.3: The question asks for two requirements. The findings state one clearly and only hint at the other.
examples.5: The question asks for two requirements. Each is stated plainly in its own claim with its source.

criteria.label: The sources fit the stakes of the question

anchors.1: Sources are anonymous, unrelated to the claim, or a restatement of another source.
anchors.3: Sources are relevant and traceable but secondary, or one claim leans on a weak source.
anchors.5: Sources are the primary or authoritative document for each claim, and each quote supports its claim.

examples.1: A technical requirement is sourced to a forum post.
examples.3: A requirement is sourced to a tutorial that summarizes the standard.
examples.5: A requirement is sourced to the standard's own text.

criteria.label: The buyer states whether the work was accepted
